"It was almost the same, only in this one I had a lost look," Carlos revealed that although NLP (natural-language processing) models are capable of incredible feats, their abilities are very much limited by the amount of context they receive. This limitation could cause difficulties for researchers who hope to use them to do things such as analyze ancient languages. In some cases, there are no contexts at all to provide.

Sarah Waters' novel "Fingersmith" also plays with the concept of context and time. Waters uses the first line of the novel to signify where she begins, cycling the story. Even the novel's language bridges this divide. Waters often employs the word "queer" to describe the unusual or remarkable, instead of its post-1922 connotations of homosexuality.

The TV show "Fondo de cultura economica" (The Economic Culture Fund), which was broadcasted on RTVE2 on April 17, 1977, is an example of how context can be crucial for understanding a work. The show featured a reading of Juan Rulfo's "¡Diles que no me maten!" ("Tell them not to kill me!") by the author himself. The recording of this reading is an important cultural artifact, providing insight into Rulfo's intonations, pacing, and interpretation of his own work.

"Asombro por Juan Rulfo" (Amazement for Juan Rulfo) is a documentary about the Mexican author's life and work, highlighting the importance of understanding the context in which an author writes to fully appreciate their work.
